request_classification.request_type: documentation-wide terminology refactor with governance safeguards

claims.claim_text: Replace 'Layer 2' and 'Layer-2' with 'truth_store' in all canonical documentation and CLAUDE.md where the terms refer to the project's architectural layer.
claims.classification_rationale: Layer 2 is documented as operational at snapshot boundary (CLAUDE.md Section 3.1: 'Layer 2 = operational at snapshot boundary'). It is a current-state architectural term with verified cross-document presence across all seven canonical sources and CLAUDE.md itself. Renaming this term is a contract-affecting documentation change to current-state truth. The term's current-state status is unambiguous and well-supported.
notes: Layer 2 / snapshot boundary is the most foundational current-state architectural concept in the system
Renaming touches the snapshot contract semantics indirectly — clarity must be preserved
CLAUDE.md Section 11 requires documentation review for contract-affecting changes

claims.claim_text: Replace 'Layer 3' and 'Layer-3' with 'decision_layer' in all canonical documentation and CLAUDE.md where the terms refer to the project's architectural layer.
claims.classification_rationale: Layer 3 is documented in the current canonical set as target architecture — NOT YET BUILT (CLAUDE.md Section 3.2). However, the rename itself is a current-state documentation change: the term 'Layer 3' currently exists in canonical docs describing planned components, phase gates, and architectural boundaries. The act of renaming a term that currently appears in documentation is a modification to current-state documentation content, even though the referent (Layer 3 functionality) is target-state. The current docs clearly and repeatedly document Layer 3 as planned/target architecture, so there is strong cross-document support for what Layer 3 means and where it appears.
notes: The subject matter of Layer 3 is target-state architecture, but the documentation entries being modified are current-state text
Touches target architecture indirectly — downstream flag set
Must preserve the NOT YET BUILT / planned status in all renamed references to avoid unsupported implementation promotion
CLAUDE.md Section 3.2 explicitly lists planned components: Feature Builder, Index Suite, Regime Gate, Supervisor Engine, Decision Engine, Execution Layer

claims.claim_text: Enforce terminology replacement as a strict naming convention only where terms refer to the project's architectural layers — do not blindly apply to all occurrences.
claims.classification_rationale: This is a scope-control constraint on the refactor itself. It aligns with the project's documentation governance model (CLAUDE.md Section 2) which requires role-matched interpretation and avoids convenience-based changes. The constraint that renames must be context-sensitive (architectural layer references only) is a sound governance principle consistent with the canonical framework. Classification as current-state reflects that it governs a change to current documentation.
notes: Requires semantic analysis of each occurrence to determine whether it refers to an architectural layer vs. an unrelated literal
Python module paths like 'layer2/' and import references like 'layer2.index_suite' must be excluded from text replacement

claims.claim_text: Do not alter unrelated literals, code module names, import paths, or historical references without governance review.
claims.classification_rationale: This safeguard directly invokes multiple canonical principles: (1) Historical source handling — CLAUDE.md Section 2.3 requires that historical documents be preserved as non-current-truth context, not silently rewritten. (2) Code conventions require no hidden side effects. (3) The rename-invariance requirement protects code module names (e.g., 'layer2/' directory, 'README_LAYER2.md' as filename) and import paths from silent breakage. The claim is well-supported by the canonical governance framework.
notes: Historical references preserved for traceability must retain original terminology with annotation if needed
Code paths like 'layer2/', 'layer2/index_suite.py' are implementation artifacts not documentation terminology
README_LAYER2.md filename is a special case — handled separately in c5

claims.claim_text: Detect whether README_LAYER2.md and any other filenames require rename handling as part of this terminology refactor.
claims.classification_rationale: README_LAYER2.md is explicitly listed as canonical document #7 in CLAUDE.md Section 2.1. It is referenced by name in CLAUDE.md Sections 2.2, 2.4, and 11. Renaming this file would constitute a contract-affecting change to the canonical document set itself, requiring updates to every cross-reference in CLAUDE.md and potentially in other canonical documents. This is the highest-impact sub-claim in this request because it affects the canonical document registry, not just document content.
notes: CLAUDE.md explicitly names 'README_LAYER2.md' at least 7 times as a canonical source
Any rename must atomically update all CLAUDE.md references, DOCUMENTATION_VERIFICATION_MATRIX_v1.md entries, and any other cross-document pointers
Filename rename has cascading governance implications — potential blocking condition
Must verify no other systems (hooks, workflows, CI) reference README_LAYER2.md by path

claims.claim_text: Fail closed if the rename would introduce ambiguity, architecture drift, or snapshot-boundary confusion.
claims.classification_rationale: Direct invocation of the fail-closed principle from CLAUDE.md Section 7: 'The system MUST default to NO OUTPUT rather than incorrect output.' Applied to documentation governance, this means the refactor must halt rather than produce ambiguous, drifted, or boundary-confused documentation. This is a core constitutional principle with the highest possible canonical support.
notes: Fail-closed applies to: ambiguity in renamed terms, architecture drift from current/target confusion, snapshot-boundary confusion from unclear 'truth_store' scoping
This principle is non-negotiable per CLAUDE.md Section 7

claims.claim_text: The refactor must produce terminology, role-citation, phase-alignment, change-impact, rename-invariance, and doc-code-sync outputs.
claims.classification_rationale: The requested output types align with the governance model described in CLAUDE.md (document update obligations in Section 11, verification matrix in Section 5, phase-gate model in Section 4). However, the specific output artifact names (terminology, role-citation, etc.) are workflow-defined rather than constitutionally specified. Classification confidence is medium because the output types are reasonable governance derivatives but their exact format is orchestration-defined, not canonically specified.
notes: These outputs correspond to downstream governance steps in the orchestration workflow
The classification step (this agent) produces claim_classification_map only — the other outputs are downstream responsibilities

possible_blocking_conditions: canonical_document_filename_rename_required — README_LAYER2.md is named in CLAUDE.md canonical set; renaming it is a contract-affecting change with cascading cross-reference updates
claude_md_self_referential_update_required — CLAUDE.md itself uses 'Layer 2' and 'Layer 3' extensively and references README_LAYER2.md by name; the refactor modifies the constitutional document

target_state_terminology_must_preserve_not_built_status — all renamed Layer 3 / decision_layer references must retain their planned/target/not-yet-implemented qualification to avoid unsupported_current_state_claim
snapshot_boundary_clarity_at_risk — replacing 'Layer 2' with 'truth_store' must not obscure the snapshot contract boundary semantics documented in CLAUDE.md Section 6
cross_document_atomicity_required — terminology must change consistently across all seven canonical docs plus CLAUDE.md in a single atomic operation to avoid verification matrix inconsistency
